To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the multi-view assumption, as formalized in this work, is a useful information theoretic principle for learning, (2) the multi-view learning problem is well-suited for the PAC style semidefinite framework and (3) canonical correlation analysis is normatively justified as a dimensionality technique for multi-view data.
(i) a natural multi-view assumption can be stated and (ii) this multi-view assumption can provide a normative basis for dimensionality reduction.
• We formalize the multi-view assumption and study the PAC style semi-supervised learning paradigm for the multi-view learning setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) Formalizing a natural multi-view learning assumption in the PAC style framework of Balcan et al. [BBV07] 2) Deriving incompatibility functions (which are used to score the goodness of hypotheses) for certain loss functions 3) Deriving performance bounds for coregularization methods 4) Providing a normative justification of CCA as dimensionally reduction technique.
the theoretical justification of the multi-view learning setting.
developing a formal information theoretic framework that allows us to analyze and design multi-view algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the information theoretic multi-view assumption is indeed a natural and useful assumption to study the multi-view paradigm.
CCA is an empirically and theoretically successful dimensionality reduction technique, when the multi-view assumption holds and the target is a convex loss function.
the multi-view learning setting can be formalized as a PAC-style semisupervised learning setting, and we provide a formal justification for several existing techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it provides a normative justification of the coregularization paradigm and shows that CCA is a natural dimensionality reduction technique in the multi-view setting.
we provide a principled information theoretic framework for multi-view learning and we show that the coregularization and canonical correlation analysis techniques fall within this framework.
we provide a formal information theoretic framework for multi-view learning, and show that many of the existing multi-view algorithms fall into this framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it shows that multi-view semi-supervised learning can be studied in the PAC framework and the results can be used to justify certain multi-view semi-supervision algorithms.
it provides a formal justification for the multi-view paradigm and shows how to derive incompatability functions that can be used to bound performance of multi-view learning algorithms.

we provide a formalization of the multi-view assumption in the semi-supervised learning paradigm and show how this formalization can be used to derive incompatibilities for certain classes of loss functions and provide normative justifications for dimensionality reduction techniques.
